subject.title: Feature: Granular Discord action gates (split actions.messages into read/edit/delete)

question: Should Discord `actions.messages` become a backward-compatible granular gate for send/read/edit/delete, and what exact public config shape should own that security boundary?
rationale: This changes a public configuration and destructive-action authorization boundary, so automation should not choose the durable config contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add object-shaped message gates
options.body: Preserve the existing boolean shorthand and add `actions.messages: { send?: boolean; read?: boolean; edit?: boolean; delete?: boolean }` as the documented granular form.

options.title: Add separate top-level gates
options.body: Keep `actions.messages` as the legacy coarse gate and add separate top-level Discord action keys for granular message controls.

options.title: Defer for cross-channel design
options.body: Keep the issue open while maintainers decide whether message action gates should become a broader cross-channel policy rather than a Discord-specific shape.

recommendation.title: Add object-shaped message gates
recommendation.body: Preserve the existing boolean shorthand and add `actions.messages: { send?: boolean; read?: boolean; edit?: boolean; delete?: boolean }` as the documented granular form.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history in the inspected Discord action/config paths and prior review context for this issue.
